utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, and good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-67-T, The Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This is Thursday, January, 24th, 2008. I welcome Ms. Dahl, Mr. Seselj, and our witness. Just a comment on the way our hearing is going to occur. We'll have a break at 1.45 and will resume at 5:00 -- and until 7.00. Exceptionally we will sit until 7.00 because normally on Thursday afternoons we will sit until 6.30. But since we have a longer break, we will sit until 7.00. Theoretically we should be able to finish this witness today. Mr. Seselj, I don't really remember how many time you have left, but I'm sure the legal officer will tell us exactly where -- where you stand, but you can start and I will tell you in due time how much time you've got left.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think, Mr. President, that I have more than an hour and a half left. I don't know exactly how many minutes, but my people are checking that. They are counting the time. At any rate, it is more than an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stoparic, the last thing that we discussed yesterday was the question of that assertion that you had made that the members of the Serb Radical Party took part in the persecution of Ivica Kopic from Gibarac in the municipality of Sid and that under duress he had to change and to -- he to move and to exchange his property. Later on you made this a bit more relative. You said that you heard about this, that you heard from someone that it had happened. However, in the statement that you gave to the OTP and that was submitted to me - and I think that you repeated that during the examination-in-chief - you said that this happened in 1992. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may present the witness with his original signed statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I may have said that in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In 1992, yes. That's why I want you to confirm that now, that you had said that. 15 minutes ago, I got a fax from Belgrade consisting of two documents. I'd like to show these two documents to you now and then you could hand them over to the Trial Chamber. One document is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. Mr. Seselj, we don't have a translation for these documents.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, I think there's no need to have them translated in their entirety. When you have a look at them you understand straight away what it is all about. The most important thing is that the year of the property exchange is clear. Ivica Kopic, or rather, his mother Anica was the owner of the house involved, signed a contract --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We saw. Ms. Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, I want to reiterate the objection I made to an improper use of documents in cross-examining a witness. It is unfair to the Prosecution and the Chamber to present documents that have not been translated and I cannot react appropriately in anticipation of the questions to be put to the witness on a document. Your guide-lines are quite clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Just a reminder, in terms of procedure, Mr. Seselj. The precedence of this Tribunal and the practice of all Trial Chambers are as follows. During cross-examination, the Defence must disclose to the Bench and to the Prosecution before the cross-examination starts all exhibits that are to be used. To make sure that these exhibits are in one of the two working languages of the Tribunal. There could be exceptional circumstances like today, where the accused suddenly receives on the fly, if I could say so, one last document. But this is really an exceptional circumstance and nothing more, and there's a reason behind this. Prosecution must have enough time to check the document, make sure it is authentic, reliable in order not to be caught by surprise. It goes -- it's exactly the same thing as when Prosecution is doing its examination-in-chief. It must disclose to Defence the list of all documents that it will use. We're supposed to have equality of arms and this is why this procedure applies and I wanted Mr. Seselj to be reminded of this. But he just told us that he got this document at the very last minute. Well, we will get it and put it on the ELMO just to see the date. Because obviously there is a problem with the date and just the date and you don't need to translate the date. Ms. Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, let me suggest that prejudice can be avoided by giving me a ten-minute recess so that I can have the opportunity to have a language assistant review the document with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, you only have one copy of this document? Your linguistic assistant is next to you, right, this legal assistant, is she next to you?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Ms. Bosnjakovic serves as my case manager. She is also language qualified and I would be willing to ask her to assist in this regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] She could just glance at the document right now. Let's take that document and hand it over to Ms. Dahl so she can look at it and the -- her case manager will glance through it and confirm.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a contract. It is a very poor copy but you can see the year when it was signed and you can see who the signatory is. It has to do with an exchange of property, immovable property. This is a much better copy. This is a decision of the municipal court in Sid. It is from the land registry office accepting the change of owner on the basis of this contract. Now why is this document important for me. It is dated from 1995, not 1992. Judge, I have two more problems, do not interrupt me now.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You cannot interrupt me now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: This should take place outside the presence of the witness. If Mr. Seselj wants to defend the -- he should not be publishing the document to the witness before anybody has had a chance. This is completely irregular. I'm sorry. It is not proper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't agree with you. Show this document to Ms. Dahl, please. It's just to check the date and the title of the document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to continue examining this witness so we don't waste any more time, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. You're asking questions. But first we're not deducting this from your time, so let Ms. Dahl read the document first. Furthermore, we could have simultaneous translation if the document is on the ELMO. So let's put the first document on the ELMO, please. That way everybody will see the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the document is completely illegible and it does not indicate whether it is a complete document. There are handwritten figures on the bottom that indicate that there are pages missing. I don't know what this means, but I'll let the Chamber look at it. But I'm unable to read it with a qualified assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we will look at it. It's the first document with a stamp, a signature. This seems to be an official document. It looks like an official document. We'll put this first document on the ELMO, please. It appears to be an authentic document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, on the second document, you can only see the names of the signatories and the year, because it is an illegible copy. It was sent by fax but it is on the basis of this document that the state authority issued the following document, so the other document is more important, because that is fully legible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first document is legible. The second document is less legible. It appears to contain a number of paragraphs and there's also a stamp. Let's put it on the ELMO to see it. The accused can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, according to the accused, it should be read first.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, if you could put an interrogatory to the accused about the source of this document and whether it was recorded in the public records and where he got it so we may know what it purports to be, because it certainly isn't an original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Seselj, please, where do these two documents come from, please?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document that you have just placed on the ELMO is the document of the municipal court in Sid. It is from its land registry department. This municipal court also has a copy of the contract that I have submitted as well. That is not particularly legible because, on the basis of that contract they issued this decision on the new register of this property. So all this can be obtained at the municipal court in Sid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll have the contract on the ELMO. It comes from the land registrar in Sid, or the surveyor's office.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, let's make a proper record and have some identification records added to these documents so that we don't lose track in the transcript of what Mr. Seselj is referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Registrar, could you please give a number for the two-page document, and a second MFI document -- number, excuse me, for the document that's just one page down and that's legible.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The two-page document that is purporting to be the land registry will be MFI D3 and the single-page document will be marked for identification as D4.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The other way around. One page is from the land registry. It's just the other way around. The one page is an excerpt from the land registry, or, rather the decision of the relevant service for land registry, and the other one is the court document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The contract is two pages long and the land registry is one page long. The document from the land registry is one page long; that is for the transcript. Mr. Registrar, so could you please give us numbers because they were not noted on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The one-page document will be marked for identification as D3 and the two-page decision will be marked for identification as Exhibit D4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's no MFI in the transcript. Mr. Seselj, you have the floor. It's a contract between two people and there is -- this is recorded in the land registry record.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, did you know Ivica Kopic from Gibarci personally?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you know where his house was?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember now but I used to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that he lived in Gibarci in the street of Marsala Tita number 10 with his wife and one child. Is that right, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in touch with Ivica Kopic in high school and I played soccer football for a while with him but later on we hardly saw each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The house that he lived in was owned by his mother, and now I would like you to either confirm this or deny this. To the best of my knowledge the house was being in the process of construction. There was electricity there but there was no water there and there weren't any bathrooms. One room had not even had plaster on the walls. Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Possibly he was building something.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, and now I'm asking you whether you know about this, he exchanged this house with Petar Vujaklija from Sotin, Sotin is a suburb of Osijek. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Sotin is a village near Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: As far as I know Osijek but perhaps you're right. It's a suburb of Osijek. It is to the north of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You may recall that you can reach Vukovar from the direction of Negoslavci and from Sotin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: To the north of Vukovar so it's near Osijek, it's not too far away Osijek from Vukovar. Previously, Vujaklija Uras moved to Kukujevci. Did you know Uras Vujaklija?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: This is going too fast and I'm not getting accurate translation, I'm sorry. They're overlapping again.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, Ivica Kopic looked up Petar Vujaklija himself, because he knew his brother Uras. Petar Vujaklija had been expelled from Osijek and he lived in Backa Palanka and he offered an exchange of houses. From the documents we can see that the exchange was carried out in 1995. Today, Ivica Kopic and Petar Vujaklija are still friends. Do you doubt that? A Croat and a Serb who exchanged property are friends to this day?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that many Croats who left the municipality of Sid come to this day, especially for the fair. You know that in Sid there is a well-known fair on the 15th day of every month and they come, so why would they not have a relationship if they had a proper exchange of houses?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In this exchange Ivica Kopic fared much better to the best of my knowledge, because the house that he got in Cepin had be completed.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: People lived there and it was fully equipped. Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Is Mr. Seselj testifying or is he asking questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, ask questions. You're testifying right now. Ask questions, ask questions. You're testifying right now. Ask questions, ask a question, ask a question to get the answer you want and put your point across to the Judge, but ask a question. Say, If I tell you that there was an exchange, that this exchange occurred in 1995, and that both partners were friends, there is a Serb on the one hand and a Croat with the other one, do you agree with me, and then he will answer, Yes I agree or, No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I did put this question to him, Mr. President. Does he doubt this information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, regarding this specific question, yes, but the next question was not a question. It was testifying.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: We are going to finish dealing with Ivica Kopic. You tired me a bit with this question. When did you met Ms. Natasa Kandic, Mr. Stoparic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Hold on, Mr. Seselj. You should not be wasting your time. If I understood you right through these documents you were saying that contrary to what we have in the written statement and what the witness said there, Kopic was not expelled but there was an exchange between two consenting parties who signed an agreement that was correctly recorded. Is that your point?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But the most important thing is that the exchange did not even take place in 1992 but in 1995, three days later in relation to what Stoparic's statement says -- or, rather, I misspoke, three years later.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I say something in this regard, Your Honours, because this question is being put to me and I'm being shown this document but I haven't said a word about this. Your Honours, this document is truthful, authentic, there is no need to doubt it, but it proves when the owner of the house exchanged his house with somebody else legally, but it doesn't prove when the Kopic family left Serbia and whether they were refugees in Croatia and then after a while legally they exchanged their immovable property. I did not say that he left in 1992. He could have left in 1993 or at the end of 1992 but there was pressure against such people. In my opinion this document shows when there was a legal exchange of houses but it doesn't show at all when he actually left Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Ivica Kopic left Serbia in 1995. Are you challenging that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I think he left earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Oh, you don't know?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, I did not see him off at the railway station. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you did know what to say to the investigators, that it happened in 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that he had some problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: No. You said that he left in 1992.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he could have left then.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, it would appear that the tone of Mr. Seselj's questions is acrimonious and he is making remarks to indicate his displeasure with the witness's answer, and I believe that is not a proper use of his right of cross-examination and I would ask for an instruction that he would refrain from mocking and expressing irritation at the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Seselj, it seems that your demonstration you were about to carry out is failing and has a flaw, because the witness says that he didn't leave in 1995. The witness doesn't exclude the fact that maybe the departure was earlier. This is where we stand. Please continue. It won't be a problem for you anyway. I'm sure you will find a witness to come to confirm your case. Move on to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: My question was, when did you met Natasa Kandic, Mr. Stoparic?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, try to remember, what year was this? I am giving you the chance to correct yourself.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you know this better than I do, please remind me. I can't remember. Perhaps it was a bit earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How much earlier? You said 2004 and then I expressed my doubt and then you say maybe it was earlier. When could that earlier have been?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when I say 2004 I mean the second half of 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, this Prosecution provided me with a document from which one can see that you made contact with Natasa Kandic in 1999 and gave the first statement to her. The Prosecution provided me with that document. I'm looking for it now. The year was 1999. You made a statement about certain circumstances which are not essential for me here at the moment but you know what's it about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Ms. Dahl. I must say that I don't really like objections. I'm trying to find the truth and the substance of this case. I don't know why you raise to your feet, but this is at least the fifth time you raise to your feet since we started. What did you want to say this time?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like the witness to be given the document that he is being examined on if the accused is asserting that he gave a statement, and we've disclosed it to the accused, I think protocol requires that the witness be treated fairly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, just wait, maybe he will give the document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have found a document dating back to 2003. That's one year before.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you frighten me. You said I said 1999 and I am sure that I didn't know her in 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You said 2004. It says 2003 here, 28th of March, 1999 so perhaps that's the mistake. Anyway, you gave the statement to her on the 31st of August, 2003. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Where did you meet her for the first time?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What was the name of the restaurant?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Hold on. Mr. Seselj, I'm stopping you here. You have a document. It may be important. I don't know what is in this document. But if this document is here to support your case, I told you already and I'll tell you again. Before cross-examination, prepare in a file for the Bench with all these documents. Hand them over, ask for a translation, if the translation hasn't been done, but obviously it looks like you already have a translation in English. And therefore, as a professional Judge, I can read the document, I can see where you're going, I can ask my own questions and it's a better use of everybody's time. Right now we're totally blind. You have a document in hand. We have no idea what this document is and you're asking questions about it. I have been here for five years and during cross-examination I was always given the documents before the cross-examination started. You're doing yourself a disservice working this way, because what you are saying will not be taken into account by the Judges when they deliberate and rule and think about the case. You have to give us the document. If you don't give us the document, you have a big problem. You're really going against your own interest.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this -- the document number is 04246788. I have absolutely no possibility of providing you with these documents in advance. Today, I wanted to photocopy a document, a one-page document, in the detention centre today and the guard told me that I had to send in a particular request to have that one page copied. Then I brought the paper here to Court and asked Mr. Doraiswamy to copy it for me and to hand it to the registry. Now, if you're asking me to see to technical matters of that nature, then it would be better to have this trial finish straight away with a judgment. I was searched twice, for example, coming from the detention centre to here and they mixed up my documents and I haven't had time to put them back in order yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm listening to what you're saying. If the Trial Chamber issued a ruling allowing you to have associates and a case manager, that was precisely for this reason, and this view for reasons I'm not going to address here, it wasn't possible to do it. We should have from the registry somebody who is made available to you who would do the photocopying at your request. That person could put together the documents into files. I believe that the registrar is very favourable to this idea. It is in everybody's interest. Otherwise, we are going to get the impression that you're like a fish in a bowl and that you are asking questions totally isolated without the Judges having the documents. You know as well as I do how powerful a document can be, what its scope can be. So it's in your interest. Have a good thought about it. Imagine that you could have somebody appointed by the registry who could, upon your instructions, do the photocopying and put together the files for cross-examination purposes. Based on that, you would come to the hearing equipped with binders that would be given to the OTP and to the Bench. In this way, you could better use the scope of your questions, make it possible for the trial Judges to understand what your aim is. Failing that, we shall continue in the same way, it's going to be a waste of time. You're going to also waste your energy, lose it. Each time Ms. Dahl will be on her feet to say that is a problem. I can't force you to anything, but think about it. Think about my proposal.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you wish me to continue, Mr. President, with the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, you have had time to think and remember what the cafe's name was.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was called Lipo Vlad.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, that is what my information tells me too. Now, how long after that first meeting did you meet Natasa Kandic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Many times.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you can't even count the number of times?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you get to know Sonja Biserko?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: After setting up closer cooperation and this friendship with Natasa Kandic, did you bring any other people in to get to know her?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Some people who were witnesses in some trials and then that they should change their testimony in cohorts with her, with agreement from her?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, I think that like you, you received a report from a western police force. I'm not going to mention it if you don't tell me to do so, but the public knows about this because it was on the Internet. It was the police of a western country which is not where Mr. Stoparic has been given refuge. Would you like me to give you the name?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're now saying that I must have a received a report. Not at all. The only things the Judges receive are the documents from Ms. Dahl's binder for the examination-in-chief and the documents that you give us, if any, because for the time being you have not given any documents, so I'm not aware of this report. So this is a surprise. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. We're going to redact. Did Mr. Seselj say that there was a police report without saying where it comes from and that there are certain facts in this report, because, you know, a police report, I mean there are 192 countries in the United Nations; it could be one of them. Please do not identify with any accuracy what this report is. What is of interest to you is the fact that, allegedly, Ms. Kandic would have gathered several witnesses. Is that the question?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not Ms. Kandic but that Mr. Stoparic brought in people to Ms. Kandic who, after talking to her, agreed to change their testimony in a specific Court. Now I'd like to draw your attention to ERN number 06247275 is the number. I hope that it can come up on e-court, that your services can put it up on e-court. That is the only way in which I can disclose the documents that I received from Madame Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour, but the insinuations by the accused are extremely serious and I object to his providing those statements without evidentiary support or intent to cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Dahl, it appears that the accused has a document which, allegedly, contains a statement by the witness saying that this witness would have brought witnesses to Ms. Kandic, and this is purported to be in the document we have just received the number of. You had asked for a private session. Maybe we can move to private session just to see this document. Mr. Registrar, can you show us this document? We could move to private session just for the time of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, I am absolutely opposed to a private session. You can see the document. I'm not going to mention the name of the man, nor am I going to mention what state is referred to here. So please don't go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The problem is that if we put or display a document on the screen, if that document can be identified by an individual whilst it was indicated that this could only be done in private session, that creates a problem. What was in private session was the question you put on the basis of this document. Ms. Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: The paper copy of the law enforcement agency report I gave the registrar's representative indicates the source of the report and its confidential nature, so it would not be appropriate to broadcast it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think that this could be put to the witness. I'm just going to quote one sentence which, in itself, says nothing with respect to the subject matter and the name of the person who Mr. Stoparic brought. Mr. Stoparic, to the police of that western country said that he personally, quite literally, had taken by the hand this -- a certain man, took him by the hand and took him to see Natasa Kandic and he confessed to Natasa Kandic, as is later said here, that he to lie earlier, but after talking to her I assume he decided to tell the truth and that is to be found on page 65. I gave you the ERN number. If you wish to go into private session, I would rather withdraw my question because I'm not interested in private sessions at all. So I will be ready to retract the question straight away if you mean to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The private session was to prevent this document from being seen outside this courtroom. If it is not put on the ELMO, nobody will see it. So we're going to show that document to the witness. Witness, please look at the document. Mr. Seselj, put your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, take a look at the third paragraph from the bottom and then the fourth sentence in that paragraph. Later on that man - don't give his name - and then start with the following, that I personally literally would take him by the hand and so on. It's the third paragraph from the bottom, the fourth sentence. The name of the man is mentioned but are you to refrain from doing so and it is on page 65, the ERN is 06247275.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to answer?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Could I ask Mr. Seselj to republish the page that he's referring to. I'm making arrangements to have a proper copy for the Chambers brought.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please. Give that number again, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page number is 65 and the ERN number is 06247275. I assume that the ERN number is more important because each side has a separate ERN number, each page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right, so the ERN number is 06247275, is that right? Whilst you were speaking the witness had a look at the text, so you can ask your question now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He has already asked the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I've already asked the question. You told this to the police of this particular western country.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the interview with the police from that western country. The interview was conducted in the following manner. Nothing was written down but there was an audiotape of the interview and I read this and was very surprised, because somewhere in this report you'll find that I am married to an Albanian woman and that's an absolute lie. I brought this to the attention of many people and warned them. Now, I'm not saying that certain police forces are prone to lying or not but they investigated something and wanted to deal with someone from their own state. And later on that man was freed. But everything was very badly translated, so --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly slow down again please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I read through this statement and it doesn't say that you married an Albanian lady but that you got to know an Albanian and that she told you how the Albanians lived in Kosovo and then afterwards you sort of saw the light.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serb judge who call me during the investigation process in a case linked to this told me precisely that I was married and then he showed me some things from this, and I told him that I was very surprised why that was so and I asked him why don't have you the audiotape what was made.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, well, I'm a little more intelligent, I assume, than that Serb judge. I don't let myself be caught in plots like that. I don't say that you're married to an Albanian woman. I'm not thinking up the contents of the transcript, so don't mix me up with that Serbian judge.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just mentioned him. I didn't know that this existed of. The only thing I knew was that there was an audiotape, an audio recording, and if this exists then an audio recording must exist and you can compare the two.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: I think that there's been a mistake in the record or perhaps Mr. Seselj's understanding. He accused Mr. Stoparic of having admitted to Ms. Kandic in this -- that he had lied and I just read the statement and the transcript of the portion that Mr. Seselj was referring to, and it says that Mr. Stoparic explained that the gentleman who we're not naming admitted that he had to lie, not that Mr. Stoparic had admitted to lying. And I think that that was the beginning of the cross-examination, and I want to make sure that there is no misleading statements made about what Mr. Stoparic has done and said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Seselj, the Prosecution says that it is Mr. X who admitted that he'd lied, not Mr. Stoparic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I precisely said so in the Serbian language, namely, that Mr. Stoparic had brought in a certain man and that that man, after talking to Natasa Kandic, admitted that he had lied and then decided to change his statement. I never said that Mr. Stoparic lied. Perhaps the interpretation is not good enough, but Mr. Stoparic remembers this and you have a recording of what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... To say that that is what I understood too in French so it was just a matter of interpretation into English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and do endeavour to speak more slowly. You see, you speak so fast that inevitably, there can be errors in the interpretation and that can also have consequences but it was very clear in French.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, this police of this western country, on the 3rd of June, 2004, you stated to them that you had become so close to Mrs. Kandic, and now I'm quoting what you said, that you had the keys to both her apartment and to her offices. That is on page 53 of your statement to the western law enforcement service. Is it true?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partially.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What does "partially" mean?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had the keys to her flat.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Meaning that you could go into her flat when she was not there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I stayed there when she was not present.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you also were there when she was present?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, also when she was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Does that mean or, rather, that means you a person in whom Madame Kandic had maximum confidence, right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if someone lets you into their flat and lets you sleep over there their flat, it is quite clear that they have confidence in you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So I'm not going to go into the nature of your relationship, but this was a relationship of maximum confidence since she gave you the keys to her apartment?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was the only way in which she could save my life because I was unable to move.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stoparic, luckily enough, your life is saved. Ms. Kandic got you in touch with people from the American embassy in Belgrade on repeated occasions, did she not, Mr. Stoparic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember one instance.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you stated it was in several instances, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I now remember one. At that time I might have recalled more. I had lots of talks. But I'm quite certain that they were people from the American embassy.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 3rd June, this western police -- you stated to this western police this, which is on page 49 of the transcript, that through the mediation of Natasa Kandic you had a number of talks with representatives of the US embassy?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I said foreign embassies but it is quite sure that one of them was the American embassy.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But here it is only stated the American embassy?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said that the audio recording should be consulted in this regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Stoparic. Let us just note that. You talked with -- to Natasa Kandic on many instances about your pending testimony in my case before it even started.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, you did. And when you started giving your testimony on the very first day, Natasa Kandic also sent you a SMS message?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I said as much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes. And she asked you how you were, right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, she did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then she told that you the radicals were wreaking chaos in Serbia, did she not?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, she did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And what conclusion did you draw from her words?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will ask her and call her only after finishing this testimony what that meant. What conclusion I had respect of this chaos statement, I don't know. She said nothing new. I'm not going into the relationship that you have or she has vis-a-vis whom she likes or doesn't like. Well, I took the message to actually mean exerting pressure on future witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Future witnesses. Was not that message actually exerting pressure on you, Mr. Stoparic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it was, it could not have frightened me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But I think you did strike one as quite frightened for a couple of days. But let us not talk about anything that might require the session to be closed.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We all know why.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, you agreed -- about your complete testimony with Natasa Kandic in my case?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... Madame Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Beginning at hour 15, minute 514 where the subject of private session previously, and I'd request the redaction of that passage. It appears Mr. Seselj has moved on to a new topic so that would be the complete portion of my request.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not understand what should be redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber has decided that the part said in public -- in open session should remain public.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Judges.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So with Natasa Kandic, you consulted with Natasa Kandic about your entire testimony in my case?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, it is true, Mr. Stoparic. But I'm quite aware of the fact that you will not admit it to -- admit to it easily. However, what happened, your testimony was way too ambitious so that you were in fact unable to remember to memorize all the falsehoods that were suggested to you and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Leave him time to answer. Otherwise, you are testifying. So --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I have not posed my question yet, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But your question might be very long and it is going to make everything more complicated. You said that your testimony was overambitious and he can say, yes, no, and then you can continue. Otherwise, Ms. Dahl is going to be on her feet and say you are testifying and then we fall back into the same problem, same procedural problem.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm not testifying. I'm actually putting a leading question to the witness, which is my right in cross-examination, and I'm precisely asking him a leading question and it is at a full discretion of the witness to state his view, to respond. I should have liked him more to have responded immediately when I ask him question rather than after your de-valuable [as interpreted] break which you gave him right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So this testimony of yours was designed, was projected to be false in its entirety in all of its aspects and then during the proofing, during the preparations which lasted for a couple of days and several days in early January, the Prosecutor's realised that there is no man alive on this planet that can remember so many falsehoods so that they actually had you focus on repeating lies only in connection of possible developments in Vojvodina and to speak about other thins as they actually unfolded according to your discretion.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you expect me to confirm it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You have to confirm it. You can deny it. You -- say yes or no and then we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not instructed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: We have already seen all the deviations you have made from your statements in both the examination-in-chief and in cross-examination and the statement which was written for you by the OTP and which you signed. However, you made the effort to memorize the lies that were suggested to you and concern Vojvodina so that now we're going to analyse those lies. First and foremost, Mr. Stoparic, you lied when you said that the Serbian Radical Party in Sid had set up a distinct paramilitary organisation by establishing platoons and squads of members of the Serbian Chetnik Movement, did you not? That was a lie, you lied?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I attended a number of meetings of the chapter of the Serbian Chetnik Movement. There were squads and platoons. I'm not going to name any people but none of these people is any longer a member of the Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you stated in your statement, Mr. Stoparic, that this was done throughout Serbia, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the absolute right to state something of the kind if it is something that I had heard from a person whom I considered competent and knowledgeable.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you talked about the setting up of Black Troikas?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was word about it in our parts. You yourself in fact once said that some local boards issued booklets of the Serbian Chetnik Movement so you were not able to control it throughout the territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But, Mr. Stoparic, this is not the same thing. Identity cards or membership cards are one thing and the forming of Black Troikas is something else, because these are liquidation groups.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, some clandestine groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: No, not secret groups. You know what Troikas -- Black Troikas have been in history.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They killed the king.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: No, they did not kill the king. That is what you said in examination-in-chief. You said that the Dragutin Dimitrijevic Apis, who was a Colonel of the former Serbian army, formed such Black Troikas.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not what I said and that is something that I seem to recollect from my memory but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I will try to refresh your memory, Mr. Stoparic. Dragutin Dimitrijevic Apis actually led the secret officers organisation called the Black Hand, which killed the King Aleksander Obrenovic in 1903, did he not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. Ms. Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: I'm consulting the transcript from Mr. Stoparic's direct examination, and these matters were conducted in private session and I believe that the cross-examination deserves the same treatment, specific reference to the official English transcript, page 2464.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but on the issue of the Black Troika, there's no reason why this should be done in private session. Continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I remember well that Mr. Stoparic asked for a private session only on account of one name. I'm absolutely not going to mention that name. So please do not allow the session to go into private session. I remember that distinctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we continue in open session, but please do not give the name.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I absolutely will not mention the name, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And the Black Troikas were established by the Chetnik movement of Draza Mihajlovic and he sent them in the Second World War to kill the collaborators of the German occupier in Belgrade, right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Afterwards, in all fairness, these Black Troikas also liquidated some communist leaders, did they not?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you say that they are associated with the Chetnik Movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, but with the Chetnik Movement from the Second World War. Let me remind you of another thing. Draza Mihajlovic sent a Black Troika to liquidate the Chetnik duke Vojvoda Kosta Pacanac because Kosta Pacanac collaborated with the Germans. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know such details.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You don't, okay. So these Black Troikas were actually suggested to you by someone who is much more versed in history than you are so that you-- so that these lies might compromise or discredit the Serbian Radical Party as having virtually -- as having practically established not only a paramilitary organisation but also terrorist groups, right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is it not the -- I never looked at it at the time as a terrorist group.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What could a Black Troika be but a terrorist group? What else would it be doing but liquidating people, right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You just said now whom they liquidated.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But who were the Black Troika supposed to liquidate?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. You're going too fast. The witness, Mr. Stoparic, Mr. Seselj is going so fast that he forgot to put a question to you but it is an appropriate question, actually. When the word "Black Troika" appears in your statement, it is you who quoted the Black Troika from your own mind or was it an investigator or somebody put that question to you? So did you mention that expression because your cultural background allows you to go back in history and pull that out of your mind, or was it an investigator or Ms. Kandic who mentioned this to you? What happened exactly? How did this come about? How was this mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the expression, the term "Black Troikas" and I know this from when I was very young, this was something that was referred to during communist times. Only within one's families, one dare not speak about these things. I don't know how the investigators would know about them. I don't know. Maybe they did. Natasa Kandic was not in contact with me. I referred to what I knew and to some of my recollections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So yourself mentioned it. Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Then it was suggested to you to sign a false statement to the effect that the boards of the Serbian Radical Party proceeded in an organised manner to intimidating citizens of Croat ethnicity in Sid and other places in Srem, didn't you? Wasn't that not the case?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Boards? This is a difficult word. It was perhaps some people.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Who gave them this task, who told them to do that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Maybe they did it of their own accord. In conditions of impunity everything went.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How come, Mr. Stoparic, that some of the alleged incidents had not been even registered at all?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, now I'm looking at myself as a Croat and, for instance, I'm subjected to certain harassment. It does not necessarily have to be physical, it can be psychological and, I am afraid to report to the police because the police is also Serbian and somehow in my mind I have already classified them as enemies somehow. This is probably -- this is what probably was the case or there were probably cases when people just did not think that they would be assisted by the Serbian authorities which does not have to be true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: By, Mr. Stoparic, I can see that you're now retracting in this regard. You said that it was not the boards that organised the intimidation. You just that a while ago.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it could have been somebody's own initiative. I never attended a session where such orders were issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, but in the examination-in-chief you repeated that you exchanged people between boards so you would go to other boards' territories as un -- to intimidate people as unknown people to the locals?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I have explained that as well. I have explained that as well. I explained how it was that I found out about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You invented all of that, didn't you? What was the year you said that I held a rally in Kukujevci?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like Mr. Stoparic to be able to answer Mr. Seselj's question. Mr. Stoparic was asked whether he had invented facts, and that accusation deserves an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Can you answer, Mr. Stoparic? Did you invent it all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I myself spoke of what I remembered, everything that was in my head, I tried to go back to those times and I put it all together. There are no inventions or at least I didn't invent anything deliberately. Whether it was a lie or not, there's the Trial Chamber to decide whether that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, I have a letter of yours here that you sent to a friend of yours. Please identify this and tell us whether this is indeed your letter or not. Don't mention the friend's name. It doesn't matter. This is your letter to a friend of yours before you emigrated?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: I'd like an opportunity before the witness is given the letter to review it. This is highly irregular.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, when a party produces a document, they must mention when -- where the document stems from. Maybe it is the person who received the letter who forwarded it to you, for instance, because let's just suppose that this letter was, for instance, stolen, that letter could not be shown or used in Court, a document that would have been obtained through a fraudulent means. Maybe a witness gave it to you or else, but have you to tell us the source of this document. Do you have the source?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. This document is from the person to whom the letter was addressed to originally. He submitted it to my legal advisors and they faxed it to me. It is Mr. Stoparic's handwriting. The Prosecutor had a look at the document, and I kindly ask you to instruct Mr. Stoparic to read the letter without mentioning the name that is stated at the beginning of the letter.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have a tab that can conceal the name I think. I think it is perfectly appropriate to have that redacted so that -- if it is appropriate to publish. But I'll let Mr. Stoparic cover the name and make sure that it is properly concealed. And I'd ask that Mr. Seselj refrain from testifying about the document and put the questions regarding handwriting and source and things like that to the witness himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, very well. The witness will therefore take a look at the letter and tell us if he recognises the letter and then Mr. Seselj will be able to put questions on the content of the letter.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, I was not testifying about the document. I was answering your question as to what the source of the document was. Please do not allow such insinuations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So now please put questions regarding the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind, Mr. Stoparic, as to read the entire letter except for the original form of address. Please read it out.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, this is it not my letter. I don't write letters ever. And it is not my handwriting. Somebody tried to copy this. I mean, even this postscript is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, I am going to submit a request for a graphology, a handwriting expert, expertise. Before Mr. Stoparic leaves the court, could he write a text in printed letters that could be used for a handwriting expertise?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I completely reject that. I'm sorry that I'm laughing, but this is really very funny. It is not my letter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not an expert, but I've been a -- involved in criminal trials for 30 years, so I have some knowledge about graphology. So when you write, do you use block letters or do you -- how do you write?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I write in the Latin alphabet. I use block letters. But, at any rate, that's not what they look like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But if you, for instance, send a letter to somebody, to a lady, will you put "madam" with a capital M or will you just write "madam" in block letters. How would you write "madam," for instance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I very rarely write letters. In this time of mobile telephones, never. I'll tell you, this letter was written -- well, I'll tell you. The man that this letter was addressed to was actually the author of this letter. He wrote it with the assistance of somebody. It is ridiculous. Quite ridiculous. This is not my letter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I notice when I look at your statement, your signature, which does not correspond to the signature on this document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question, actually, regarding this letter. In Serbian, do you write usually in Cyrillic or in Latin characters? Which characters do you use?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I almost always use the Latin alphabet when I write.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Seselj, why do you think that the letter comes from the witness? What tells you that you're not manipulated, for instance, by the person who sent you this letter?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, yesterday I showed you in closed session the statement of a certain individual, 11 pages long. That's the man to whom this letter was addressed and this man is going to be a Defence witness for my Defence and he testifies that this is an authentic letter that he received from Mr. Stoparic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something? I'm being accused here of having written a letter, which I never -- I mean, I never wrote a letter to this man, not then, not before that, nor will I ever write him a letter. Now, whether this gentleman is going be a witness here or not, that is his own affair. When he is a witness here then he can establish everything. It is not right, since his name was not disclosed, for me to give my opinion of this man now. I'm simply not going to do anything about it now, but I tell you, when he comes, ask him about this letter. Ms. Dahl will be able to cross-examine him about that letter, and as Mr. Seselj says, I agree, I agree to be subjected to some specialist from the police with regard to this particular matter. I mean, I even agreed to Mr. Seselj choosing the expert and then we'll see whether I wrote something this nebulous. It is not my handwriting, not at all, nor do I have the habit of writing in that order. I write in a different way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now let's set aside the fact whether you're the author of the letter or not. What I'm interested in actually is the content of the letter. Would you be able to read the content of the letter, Mr. Seselj, just to see what the relevance is. If it is completely irrelevant, then there is no problem.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I absolutely deny that I wrote this and I do not allow this to have this signed of nebulous thing read out in public and in this way to besmirch my name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the majority voted - I say majority because we have a dissenting opinion - but the Trial Chamber decided that Mr. Seselj should not read the contents of this letter. So the letter will be given back to Mr. Seselj, who will then use that letter and show it to his witness when his witness is called to the bar. Is that what you wanted to say, Ms. Dahl?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like it marked for identification and I'd like a copy and I'd also request that I receive a copy of the statement Mr. Seselj just mentioned, because that was neither marked nor copied for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, this letter, would you like it to be tendered so that we can get -- so that we can give it an identification number?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the letter is read out. Why would it be admitted into evidence if it wasn't read out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I also think that I can appeal to you to decide that I be subjected to this kind of expertise, because I cannot go home in peace now, having been accused of this. I really want expertise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber will look at the problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: It's a very serious matter to perpetrate a fraud on the Court and I don't think that the document should remain unmarked and outside the record by Mr. Seselj's wish. He is brought it into Court, he has referred to it. I with like it marked and I want a copy and we will wait and see whether the individual who purports to have received such a letter and identified the author shows up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This Trial Chamber voted by a majority, because I have a dissident opinion, is asking the trial clerk to mark this document for identification. But I would like to mention the following. It seems to me, to my eyes, that it is impossible to tender a document of which Judges don't know the content. This is what I wanted to say. So, Mr. Registrar, please give a number for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that will be MFI D5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much. Please proceed, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, you mentioned that in the summer of 1991 I held a rally in Kukujevci, is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rally in Kukujevci, there was a rally in Kukujevci.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, you said on the 16th of January during the examination-in-chief that this took place in the summer of 1991?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It's in the transcript. It's the beginning of the hearing on the 16th of January?.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, would you kindly check this in the transcript. I noted it down that Mr. Stoparic said that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I always said that I was very bad with dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, however, according to the information of the Serb Radical Party, I visited Kukujevci on the 15th of May, 1993. And that is when a public meeting was held, like in hundreds of other villages, in the area of Vojvodina. This is 1993 and 1994. So you made a mistake in terms of two years. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, I made a mistake with the date. But as for what I described, you may recall I said that there was even a lunch organised at the school or was it just a speech and some conference. I described what it looked like. This is to say whether it on that date or not, I always cautioned about that, that I do not remember dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes. But you said that Jovica Stegic, the owner of Lasta agency, that was a real estate agency involved in the exchange of real estate, was a sponsor of the Serb Radical Party and organised that lunch in Kukujevci?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that. I'm sure that he was a sponsor, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I have photocopies here from Jovica Stegic's military booklet. We can place this on the overhead projector.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, this is a photocopy of the page where his name is referred to and this is the photocopy of the page where it is obvious that from the 4th of March until the 18th of August, 1993 he participated in the war and that he was a soldier in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, the individual whose booklet this apparently is, the name isn't appearing on the transcript and I haven't seen the document nor have I been provided with copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, would you be able to give the name of this person and could you please spell the name so that it can be written in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] J-o-v-i-c-a, S-p-e-g-i-c-e diacritic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. The transcript was not able to jot it down. Ah, here it is. Mr. Seselj, could you please repeat your question. We now have the document on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, from this document, can you see that it is impossible that Jovica Stegic was in Kukujevci at the same time when I spoke publicly there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by the documents, it is impossible, but in practice, that wasn't how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In practice that wasn't how it was. Does that mean that the documents are lying?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Let me explain. I'm sorry, I didn't know I was interrupting you. The documents don't lie but it is no secret that people who lived in Serbia dealt with business of varying -- various kinds, were in business, and since they were military conscripts, they were always recorded as members of some units so that they wouldn't be answerable. Now, Mr. Seselj, since you have photocopied this booklet, I'd like to see the first page, because I could recognise the man, if I saw his photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, you'll recognise him on the screen when he comes in to testify as a Defence witness. Anyway, Jovica Stegic, on the 14th of January, 2008, gave a statement which was certified by the competent authorities in Serbia in which he refutes everything that you said here. Would you hand out this statement, please, copies for the Trial Chamber, for Mr. Stoparic, and the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: It violates the Chamber's guidelines that were reiterated in Court when Mr. Seselj began his cross-examination. If he's going to confront or put to the witness information that is from someone else it is to come in the form of a question about the information, not concerning another individual and if this is anything like the other statements that were distributed, they're not under oath, they're not judicial interrogatories and they're not in a working language of the Tribunal. I'm very disadvantaged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The problem is the following: This person who, according to the witness, would have been present, and this is what he said in his written statement, would have apparently been elsewhere -- is purported to be elsewhere while he was supposed to be here, and the accused managed to obtain a statement from the person in question, which confirms the argument presented by the accused. The document is in Cyrillic, however, and I myself am not capable to translate, but Mr. Seselj will be able to put a question and will be able to tell us what paragraph he is referring to so that we can get a translation and the interpreters who know Cyrillic will be able to translate it for us. So please put your question, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, have you been given the document?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Would you please read out loud paragraph 4 of that document.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, it's very difficult for me to read any of your documents after that letter I saw a moment ago because I can't believe that anything like that could have happened to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, if it's difficult for you, do your best to overcome the difficulty.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Your Honour, this is not proper procedure. I cannot react appropriately --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The procedure is I am the one who decides on the procedure when it comes to the presentation of the evidence. So, Mr. Seselj, please read paragraph number 4 in your language and the interpreters will tell us what it is about.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jovica Stegic in paragraph 4 states as follow: I'm not, as Mr. Stoparic claims, from Srem but with my family I settled from Zagreb on the 1st of February, 1992. My family exchanged without -- sight unseen a house in Zagreb for a house in Kukujevci - and I would like to underline this in particular - a house in Zagreb for a house in Kukujevci, so a house in a major city such as Zagreb for a house in an out-of-the way village. The value of the land that we had in Zagreb was at least three times greater than the property which we were given in Kukujevci. When the exchange had taken place, I and my family did not even know where Kukujevci was. My mother is a Croatian lady from Zagorje, but because she was married to a Serb, she was sacked in the company she had worked for and this happened six months before she was supposed to retire and because of threats which she was exposed to on a daily -- which my family was exposed to on a daily basis. She was forced to enter into this exchange and exchange her property for the first person that offered it without knowing where they were going or what property awaited them over there. Now, my question to you is this: Mr. Stoparic, for 15 years you have known Jovica Stegic, is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what he claims.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know him for that many years? Have you known him for that many years? Perhaps you know him longer, not for a shorter period of time.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know him by sight and in talking to him on a couple of occasions. When I say I know someone, it means that I visit them in their home and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, you can't go home visiting with all your acquaintances.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's why I said, and if you provided me with a photograph, I could have told you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: However, Mr. Stoparic, you and Jovica Stegic just don't agree on one single detail. You claim that you knew him in 1991 and that he sponsored a lunch in my honour in Kukujevci on the occasion, whereas he claims that he arrived only in 1992. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we've already discussed that and I said he sponsored the Kukujevci lunch, but, you see, I couldn't remember the exact date, so you shouldn't take dates. I'm not a lawyer, I'm not a spy to record all the dates. That's just how it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now why --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Hold on, Mr. Seselj, we're going to have a break. First the registrar must give the military booklet a number. Mr. Registrar, could we please have a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Second question, Mr. Seselj. This hearing, you know, about the apartment and you've just read out the fourth paragraph, do you also went to tender this document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
