So the commander of a village, whether it is a Croatian village controlled by the Croatian army or a Muslim one controlled by the Muslim army or a joint one, they cannot take this risk. If they know that, we would be putting in an attack. Even if they are not aware of that being planned if in the morning they hear the roar of the shelling, they take the precautionary measure of evacuating their own civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now today Mr. Seselj asked you about the presence of Radical Party volunteers in Livno. Is it your understanding that Mr. Drazilovic was in Livno with volunteers in -- I'm sorry, that Mr. Novacic was in Livno in April 1992 with Radical Party volunteers?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you say Novacic I -- that rings the bell -- that actually reminds me of the name of a colonel. Is that whom you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let me give you his full name, Radovan Novacic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, at this point I don't remember anything. Have you not actually jogged my memory. I'm not quite sure what it is that you're asking me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know whether Mr. Radovan Novacic commanded the volunteers in Livno in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No person by that name was my commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: No, the commander of the volunteers in Livno.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no. It is not possible in Livno, because the Serb troops never marched into Livno. Perhaps some part of the Livno valley, or some villages there. I cannot say. I don't know that he commanded someone there. He was not my commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Seselj asked you today whether you had received bribes from the Office of the Prosecutor. Can you confirm or deny that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I expected such a question from Mr. Seselj, but not from you. What bribe are you talking about? The fact that I received a certain sum from the Victims and Witness Protection Unit was so that I could actually -- to tide me over until I found some employment or another source of livelihood, but this is not for that -- for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Stoparic, I'm sorry, when Mr. Seselj asked you the question, he moved to another topic before you answered; and I want to make sure the record was clear whether he had ever been offered or received any improper payments in connection with your appearances before this Tribunal or your providing factual information arising out of your knowledge of events under investigation by the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never asked for any pecuniary remuneration for anything nor did anyone offer my anything of the kind. Quite simply the answer is, no and of course you are perfectly aware of this yourself. You're asking me to speak about things that everybody knows are untrue.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point, I would conclude our examination, and I would move into admission of evidence all of the exhibits that we had marked for identification with Mr. Stoparic's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you have finished the judges would like to ask a few questions. My colleague would like to put a question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Sir, you told us that the civilian populations of the villages where you were operating were not expelled by your units. But you also mentioned mixed villages where there was a Serbian population mixed with a non-Serb population. This is what I would like to know. Regarding the Serb population, were they also evacuated, were they fleeing, or was it only the non-Serb civilian population that was concerned?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually when or if, rather, we took a village or a hamlet or any inhabited place it was not just my unit that participated, and it doesn't matter whether at that point I am a volunteer or a member of the army of Republika Srpska. So this was a coordinated action of a number of units, and we entered the village, in which village there remained both the Serbian civilians, Serbian inhabitants, and a part of Croatian population that did not leave with their own withdrawing troops and army. Immediately after that, our command established defence lines in order to prevent the enemy from seeking overnight to return to their positions, and the very next day we seek to establish civilian authorities not to have military rule and the troops then are sent forward or on. The moment the civilian authorities are established there is also set up the Red Cross and other agencies and the civilians are no longer our problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But the non-Serb civil population, were they fleeing?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually, usually they would withdraw when their army would withdraw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But they were withdrawing because they were frightened by your units, or is it because your enemy managed to convince those people to leave, to flee?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before we would take a town or village, now we're talking about someplace that we don't really know, they lived in a situation where their police and army was in control. Now, while we take the village, within two hours or so they're supposed to agree it our control. Everyone had their own reasons. They were afraid. I would never agree if the Croatian army would attack the village where I live, and my army would be withdrawing because they overpowered by the enemy, because my army was defeated by the enemy, I will withdraw together with my army. As a civilian I would not remain there at the mercy of the enemy army because I never know what they might do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much for this answer. One more thing on another topic. Did you personally feel that there was a -- an ethnic difference between you, the Croats and Bosnian Muslims, or did you have such a perception that you only perceived a difference in religion between you and them?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know that we have different religions. I know that we were warring parties, and in me there was each a dose of hatred against these people, just like they hated me. I'm talking about that period, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you say that hatred was present. Was it hatred towards people belonging to another ethnic group or people having a different religion; or was it because there were people who had a different ideology?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything that you mentioned within a single framework.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. I hope that we are not exploiting the interpreters. I have just one question to you and that is to explain to us the purpose for which volunteer militia groups were established rather than just incorporating everybody into the JNA. Were there different functions undertaken by the different volunteers groups, or why was there an army and then next to the army, a number of militias.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're calling the volunteers militias, or do you consider them be some paramilitary units or something? I'm never inclined to talk about paramilitary units because I think that was a very rare occurrence in our parts. I think that every unit has some kind of control.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I apologise for being imprecise. I'm referring to all units operating outside the army.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they could not operate outside the army, not at the time of the JNA, which, later on, no longer participated in those areas. In the area of Republika Srpska-Krajina and in the area of Republika Srpska their national armies were established. That is to say that every volunteer unit there would fall under their control or the control of the police or their Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Were there any difference in the functions they undertook compared to the functions undertook by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All commands and all the technical equipment is what was received from the JNA. It's the JNA that was the creator and the command. I can be a member of a volunteer unit, but I cannot do anything of my own accord, on my on bat. I can, as an individual, until someone catches me, sees me, and then I'm disciplined. Because also it is very difficult to attack a village if you do not have support from the JNA. Everything has to be coordinated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, your testimony is now completed. I wish you a safe journey back home. Before we adjourn, I remind everybody that we will start on Tuesday at 8.30 next week, and according to the Prosecution schedule, we shall have Mr. Tomic, your expert witness. Is that so, Ms. Dahl?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And if I may reiterate my request to admit the documents marked for identification. I believe the number range is P22 through P30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We shall rule on that. So, sorry to the interpreters. It's already ten past 7.00 but we had to finish. We couldn't do it any other way. I wish you all a very good evening. We shall reconvene on Tuesday. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 29th day of January, 2008, at 8.30 a.m.
